title: Count Basie's first Savoy appearance
summary: He was at the Savoy when Basie arrived with a book of three sheets playing blues all night; Ramirez preferred the arrangements of Teddy Hill and Harlem bands.

story.theme_name: Playing with Count Basie: joining, leading, leaving
story.community_name: Playing with Count Basie: the band, its feel and its people

blocks.x: Did the band work steadily, or did you have layoffs?
Between the Apollo and the Savoy.
Because I was at the Savoy when Count Basie came to town the first time.
Oh. And what did you think?
He ...(?)... the piano then. He had no book. He only had three pieces of music, three sheets. The whole band, that's all they had. They just played the Blues all night.
And what did you think of that?
Well, I didn't particularly like it, because

I... I could understand them just playing the Blues all night long. And Teddy Hill had this beautiful book that they were playing, you know. Teddy had a really gorgeous book, with Roy Eldridge, you know, and Chu Berry... He had a nice little band, you know, and he had beautiful arrangements! And most of the guys, you know, the bands in this city had arrangements! Don Redman, Fletcher, Benny Carter. When John Hammond came... I used to say... We used to snicker, you know, say, "Count Basie brought this big Rock-and-Roll band here" -- we were the first ones to say it! Of course, in those days there was no such thing as Rock-and-Roll. But it was a Blues band.
But that's not saying the men weren't good. They just weren't playing the music that...
Well, it was fairly raggedy, too, when it first came, wasn't it?
Well, it wasn't raggedy with what they were playing. But you just cannot play the Blues all night! You see...
Even if you've got a lot of different tempos.
